text.p: Bonds closed mixed after a session devoid of external factors, but traders said that the longer end looked generally better supported than the Spanish equivalent.
As a result, the 10-year spread could narrow from the five basis points, down from seven, at which it closed on Tuesday.
The greatest trading interest, however, could be focused on the shorter end with investors betting on a good June inflation figure and a cut in official rates sooner rather than later.
"The 10-years narrowed the spreads with the Bund and the Bonos...(and) could gain another two basis points on both tomorrow," said one trader.
Another trader said that there was a sale order by one end-user at the longer end of the curve but it should be easily absorbed.

Traders said the triple auction of 15 billion escudos each of three, five and 10 year bonds announced by the Institute for Public Credit Management did not have any great impact as the amounts were considered digestible by the market.
The spread between the two and the 10 year bonds widened to 105 basis points from 103 on Monday.
